detail.title: Multivariate uncertainty and distributional transmission
detail.abstract: Macroeconomic policy increasingly requires assessments of risk rather than point forecasts alone. This paper develops a framework to compute impulse responses for scenario probabilities and the full predictive distribution of macroeconomic outcomes. The approach combines a regime-dependent mixture VAR with endogenous state probabilities and heteroskedastic shock identification, complemented by sparse sign and narrative restrictions. Applied to the euro area and U.S., the framework addresses a central policy question following the outbreak of the 2026 Iran war: do geopolitical shocks imply a return to the risk profile observed after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, or is this time different? Results show that shocks differ not only in their effects on expected outcomes, but also in how they reshape scenario probabilities, tail risks, and transitions into high-volatility states.

title: Reserve Asset Competition and the Global Fiscal Cycle
affiliations: Kellogg School of Management and New York University (NYU) - Department of Finance

detail.title: Reserve Asset Competition and the Global Fiscal Cycle
detail.abstract: Governments tend to increase their borrowing at the same time, giving rise to a global fiscal cycle. This global fiscal cycle has a large component that is unexplained by global business cycle variables. We propose a novel explanation for the emergence of the global fiscal cycle: governments' competition over the provision of reserve assets gives rise to strategic complementarity in the issuances, even when the reserve assets are substitutes in partial equilibrium. We show our reserve-asset-competition channel explains economically significant common variation in fiscal variables, beyond the common variation induced by correlated business cycles. In doing so, our model of reserve asset demand and supply also shines light on the sources of variation in the convenience yields and seigniorage revenues earned on government debt.

detail.abstract: Investments in Industry 4.0 technologies are largely expensed under current reporting standards, leaving a firm's technological capability unobservable on the balance sheet, and voluntary disclosures about that capability are discounted as cheap talk. We examine whether third-party certification resolves this gap, using the World Economic Forum's Lighthouse designation, which certifies operational capabilities that financial statements cannot convey. Using a propensity-scorematched sample and an event-study design, we find that designation reduces trade accounts receivable, expands market share, and shifts customer composition toward ESG-oriented and developed-country buyers. These benefits concentrate among firms with lower accrual quality, smaller size, and thinner analyst coverage, though not uniformly across outcomes. Because financial reporting conveys operational capability at no level of quality, this pattern reflects not substitution between information sources but the greater weight counterparties place on a capability signal when other sources leave reliability unresolved.

detail.abstract: This article examines the positions and reservations set forth by Latin American member countries - specifically Chile, Colombia, and Mexico in the 2025 update to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Model Tax Convention. As part of a series reviewing regional responses to evolving international tax standards, the study analyzes how these jurisdictions balance compliance with OECD frameworks against the preservation of domestic source-taxing rights. Key findings highlight notable policy shifts, including Chile’s expanding reservations regarding remote work permanent establishments (PEs), fees for technical services, and indirect capital gains; Colombia’s recategorization of former non-member reservations into member positions alongside strategic positions on service PEs and Pillar One transfer pricing adjustments; and Mexico’s targeted modifications concerning interest definitions and Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP) time limits. By systematically evaluating these individual updates across treaty provisions - ranging from Article 1 to Article 29 - this paper details the legal and administrative implications for cross-border transactions and treaty negotiations involving Latin American markets.

detail.abstract: This article examines the primary positions and modifications stated by Argentina and Brazil in the December 2025 update to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Model Tax Convention. Operating as non-member accession candidates, both jurisdictions provided updated positions regarding treaty text and commentary, reflecting distinct strategic paths toward international tax alignment. The paper analyzes Argentina’s significant policy shift toward substantial convergence with OECD standards, evidenced by the reversal of long-standing positions on independent personal services, restricted force of attraction, PE definitions, capital gains taxation, and mutual agreement procedures. Conversely, Brazil’s updates present a bifurcated approach: integrating the Authorized OECD Approach (AOA) and Article 9(2) corresponding adjustments following domestic transfer pricing reform, while simultaneously reinforcing source-based taxation via broadened definitions for software royalties, bareboat charter leases, and expanded PE negotiation triggers. The comparative analysis illustrates how regional economic policy shifts, domestic law reforms, and OECD accession dynamics influence international tax treaty policy in Latin America.

title: Less Is More? Selective Visual Attention to High-Importance Regions for Multimodal Radiology Summarization

detail.title: Less Is More? Selective Visual Attention to High-Importance Regions for Multimodal Radiology Summarization
detail.abstract:
oindent	extit{Background and Objective:} Automated radiology report summarization aims to distill verbose findings into concise clinical impressions, but existing multimodal models often struggle with visual noise and fail to meaningfully improve over strong text-only baselines in the FINDINGS $	o$ IMPRESSION transformation. We challenge two prevailing assumptions: (1) that more visual input is always better, and (2) that multimodal models add limited value when findings already contain rich image-derived detail.
oindent	extit{Methods:} We introduce ViTAS (Visual-Text Attention Summarizer), a multi-stage pipeline that combines ensemble-guided MedSAM2 lung segmentation, bidirectional cross-attention for multi-view fusion, Shapley-guided adaptive patch clustering, and hierarchical visual tokenization feeding a vision transformer. We performed controlled ablations on the MIMIC-CXR benchmark and evaluated the generated impressions with BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, METEOR, CheXbert and RadGraph, together with an expert human evaluation.
oindent	extit{Results:} Selectively focusing on pathology-relevant visual patches rather than full images yields substantially better performance. ViTAS achieves 29.25\% BLEU-4 and 60.83\% ROUGE-L, improved factual alignment in qualitative analysis, and the highest expert-rated human evaluation scores.
oindent	extit{Conclusions:} Our findings demonstrate that \emph{less but more relevant} visual input is not only sufficient but superior for multimodal radiology summarization.\end{abstract}

detail.abstract: Stablecoin issuers as non-bank financial intermediaries (NBFI's) create USD substitutes (monetary liabilities) and collect subsequent deposits which are invested in short-term debt instruments for the sake of balance sheet maintenance and public confidence in their digital tokens. As more stablecoins are issued, the balance sheets of their NBFI's expand, representing increased market demand for short-term safe financial assets. Focusing on the channel of USDT's and USDC's influence on 3-month U.S. T-Bill rates, this paper examines the reallocation of public-to-private financial rents from stablecoins' USD substitute money creation. The outcome variables of interest, novel for the literature, are the two financial rent measures of U.S. seigniorage from (Cutsinger and Luther, 2022): 1) Opportunity Cost Seigniorage (OCS), the implied liquidity premium accrued to the U.S. government from its monetary base and 2) Net Revenue Seigniorage (NRS), the Fed's net interest income before remittance to the Treasury.

detail.abstract: This article challenges the characterization of international financial centers (IFCs), often called "tax havens," as enablers of tax evasion and money laundering. Drawing on an extensive analysis of tax treaties, regulatory statutes, and historical literature, we explore the evolution of the global information exchange network, its impact on integrating IFCs into the global financial system, and the resulting curtailment of their use for illicit purposes. The expansion of treaties, from Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties (MLATs) to Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) and multilateral frameworks like the OECD's Common Reporting Standard (CRS), has significantly limited the potential for secrecy-driven financial activities across all jurisdictions around the world. We also examine the regulatory transformations within IFCs generated in part by these standards, highlighting the rise of licensing systems, independent regulatory bodies, and compliance-driven practices. By focusing on how the regulatory and treaty networks have evolved to restrict financial opacity and facilitate international cooperation, we show that reputable IFCs today function no less than larger onshore centers as compliant financial hubs rather than as enablers of financial misconduct. This nuanced view suggests that the global financial architecture, while imperfect, has come a long way to create value and to increase resiliency by disrupting the use of "sunny places" by "shady people."

detail.abstract: Do changes in environmental legislative stringency affect firms’ real activities and the pollution allocation? We construct a text-based index of U.S. state environmental legal stringency from 2000 to 2021, capturing the breadth and punitive severity of newly enacted or amended environmental provisions, including monetary penalties and jail terms. Linking this index to facility-level pollution, we show that state-level legal stringency reduces corporate pollution; a Bartik shift-share instrument supports a causal interpretation.  This reduction in pollution is associated with higher cost of goods sold, lower gross margins, and greater capital expenditure. Within multi-state firms, increases in HQ-state legal stringency spill over to neighbouring-state facilities, with the pollution response differing by financial constraints and becoming more pronounced in lower-stringency states. Environmental laws therefore shape firms’ operations, internal resource allocation, and the geographic distribution of environmental externalities.

detail.abstract:
This paper studies why, in poor countries, units of 10 to 49 people hold little employ-
ment relative to units of 2 to 9, and less the poorer the country. It builds a model in
which a firm hires its relatives freely but pays a price in labor to verify anyone else.
Given the fixed cost of verification, no firm chooses a size just above that of its family.
One price per income group, fitted to this shortfall alone, also generates the collapse
of employment in units of 50 or more and the level of informality. The fitted price is
1.8 times as high in the poorest income group as in the richest. A tax on employment
beyond the family, calibrated the same way, generates both but piles firms at 5 to
9 people, where finer size classes show a shortfall. Where the price is higher, the
owner’s family more often runs firms of 50 or more. In the model, cheaper verification
moves employment within a year and who manages over a decade. After reforms
that cut the cost of registering a business, employment outside wage work falls, and
all of the fall is in unpaid family work.

detail.abstract: Can tradable regulatory claims undermine the activity regulation is designed to promote? We study India’s Priority Sector Lending Certificate market, where banks can satisfy lending mandates by purchasing regulatory credit without acquiring the underlying loans. Trading allows banks to separate regulatory attributes from balance-sheet lending and reallocates compliance toward institutions with comparative advantage. This lowers the real cost of meeting regulatory targets, but it also reduces incentives to originate qualifying credit. The results reveal a fundamental policy tradeoff: markets for regulatory claims improve compliance efficiency while potentially weakening the real activity that regulation seeks to encourage.

detail.abstract: The constant-growth perpetuity fails when nominal growth reaches the discount rate: the factor 1/(r − g) becomes infinite at g = r and undefined beyond it. This paper shows that the failure is an artifact of the implicit assumption that the firm never ceases to exist. When each cash flow is weighted by the probability that the firm survives to generate it, the terminal-value factor under a constant exit hazard h becomes, to first order, 1/(r − g + h). The singularity moves from g = r to g ≈ r + h, a boundary that can be measured. Under an extrapolated Weibull curve the domain of convergence depends on the shape parameter; under the tail convention used in practice, a hazard frozen at the last observed age, it depends only on that terminal hazard. The framework is tested on two public registries. In nineteen US sectors (BLS Business Employment Dynamics, establishment survival, 1994 cohort followed for 31 years), every sector shows decreasing hazard (k between 0.60 and 0.74); the tail hazard projected from a curve fitted on ages 0–20 differs from the observed hazard at ages 21–31 by 0.62 percentage points on average, a broadly consistent but imprecise projection; and a constant hazard estimated over the full observed lifetime overstates the tail hazard by a factor of 1.5 to 2, depending on the estimator. In Japan (1,397,101 corporations incorporated after October 2015, National Tax Agency registry), the observed legal-exit hazard is approximately flat from the first year onward (k = 1.03), so that for legal exit the exponential approximation appears reasonable without a tail convention; the evidence does not establish a constant hazard for economic exit. Comparing five survival specifications on the same data, the paper finds that only a constant hazard or a hazard frozen at the tail gives a value at g ≥ r that is finite and stable: the pure Weibull form either keeps the singularity at g = r (k < 1) or converges to values without economic meaning (k > 1), and in Japan a change in the truncation of the first year of data switches between the two. The paper closes with a four-step procedure for valuers who meet a conditional nominal growth rate equal to or above the discount rate.

detail.abstract: On 25 September 2026, Provisional Measure No. 1,394 prohibited the exploitation, offering and advertising of fixed-odds betting in Brazil, ending a regulated market that had operated since January 2025. This essay sets aside the polarised debate between economic freedom and public health to ask a prior, economic question: what happens to household income when it stops circulating through commerce, industry and services and begins to flow to betting platforms? Drawing on official data from the Central Bank of Brazil and the Ministry of Finance, and on estimates by the Celso Furtado Centre, the University of São Paulo's Made research centre, the National Confederation of Commerce and the Institute for Health Policy Studies, it distinguishes gross wagers from households' net loss, places that loss between a floor of roughly R$ 35 billion and a ceiling of R$ 62.5 billion for 2025, and traces where the retained revenue goes: modest tax collection, negligible formal employment, and profits that may be remitted abroad. It then confronts the classic 'mere transfer' objection of gambling economics and argues that, given the asymmetry of multipliers, the compromised nature of the bettor's choice and the externalities borne by third parties, the transfer is not neutral. The essay closes by examining the legal risks of the ban, including migration to illegal markets, compensation claims and the constitutional regime of provisional measures, and concludes that the measure's success will depend less on its text than on the State's capacity to prevent that income from merely changing address.

detail.abstract: In the New Keynesian model the probability that a firm leaves its price unchanged is a constant, calibrated at low inflation and used wherever the model is applied. Firms reprice more often when inflation is high, but how much more often has not been measured as a rate. That rate is the half-life of price stickiness, the trend inflation rate at which the probability has fallen by half. On the micro price-setting record of nine countries over five decades, from deflation to hyperinflation, it is about 35 percent a year, and single economies depart from it widely. The probability falls within countries, not only across them, and it falls early: by 25 percent inflation it is about two fifths below its value at 2 percent. A menu-cost model calibrated at low inflation erodes stickiness later and loses the price cuts the data keep at moderate and high inflation. A constant parameter leaves the model without a steady state at moderate inflation, because price dispersion diverges. Letting stickiness erode pushes that boundary several times further out, and at a markup of 20 percent it turns the flattening of the Phillips curve under trend inflation into a steepening.

detail.abstract: How does targeted industrial policy affect the allocation of specialized labor across firms? Using the CHIPS and Science Act as a quasi-natural experiment, I find that treated firms that are likely to receive capital subsidies and tax incentives increase employment following the policy, while closely related but untreated firms experience declines, consistent with a reallocation of labor rather than uniform job creation. These effects are strongest within narrowly defined industries and among firms competing for similar inputs. To interpret these findings, I develop a simple model in which firms compete for a fixed pool of skilled labor and, capital and labor are complementary. A subsidy that lowers the cost of capital increases the marginal value of labor for treated firms, leading to worker reallocation across firms. The results highlight a policy-induced labor reallocation channel and suggest that industrial policy may reshape the distribution of economic activity without increasing aggregate employment.

detail.abstract: The models that drive bank decisions are increasingly non-deterministic, vendor-managed, and composed from components that change independently. Outputs will shift between validation events. In April 2026 the US banking agencies replaced SR 11-7 with SR 26-2, and placed generative and agentic AI outside its scope, while leaving institutions with the obligation of governing them. This paper specifies how an institution can meet that obligation. The Vetting Contract is a bilaterally negotiated, approved, machineenforceable agreement between Risk/Governance and the Model Implementation Team that names what is vetted, declares the rules of engagement, and is enforced by machinery. It replaces periodic validation with continuous vetting as a standing discipline. It is grounded in the discipline of Risk Control Objectives; is explicit about model definition, separating deterministic calculation from behavior that needs continuous vetting; and it enables human authority through declared gates approved by risk managers rather than code releases. Every artifact is typed and closed-vocabulary, so language models can draft and explain Contracts, but no value in a Contract ever originates with a model; a person signs what validates. The contribution is structural, not technological: the architecture gives practices institutions already follow a manageable, auditable shape that machinery can act on and an examiner can read.

detail.abstract: Inflationary episodes reshape the risk-return calculus of virtually every asset class, but real estate and residential rental property in particular has long been regarded as a natural hedge against rising price levels. This article examines the mechanisms through which rental income streams adjust to inflationary pressure and evaluates the extent to which these adjustments preserve real returns for property investors. Drawing on established real estate finance literature, the paper analyzes lease structure, rent indexation practices, vacancy dynamics, and the pass-through of operating costs as determinants of inflation resilience in rental markets. The discussion situates residential and commercial rental sectors within a broader inflation-hedging framework, contrasting short-lease residential markets where rents reprice frequently with long-lease commercial markets, where indexation clauses and renewal timing determine the speed of adjustment. Illustrative comparative data and stylized figures are presented to summarize how lease structure shapes the completeness of inflation pass-through. The article concludes that while rental real estate offers meaningful inflation protection relative to fixed-income instruments, the strength of that protection is conditional on lease duration, local supply elasticity, and macroeconomic policy response, echoing findings that real estate's hedging capacity is neither uniform nor unconditional.

detail.abstract: I extend the approach of Wooldridge (2023, 2025) to allow for heterogeneous gains to treatment in the context of staggered interventions for non-binary treatments. I show that an extended two-way fixed effects estimator identifies the cohort/time dose-response function under standard no anticipation and conditional parallel trends assumptions and a selection restriction on how the gain from treatment-as measured by heterogeneous slopesis related to the level of treatment. The framework allows for covariates and easily accommodates cohort-specific trends. Moreover, event-study type approaches can be used to determine whether parallel trends appears to be violated (after allowing for heterogeneous slopes and flexible trends as a function of covariates). The treatment can be represented as a scalar or vector, and may be (roughly) continuous, discrete, or some mixture. title: Sensitization, delay discounting, and BMI percentile change over 24 months in adolescents from lower-income households
affiliations: State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo, State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo, State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo, State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo and University at Buffalo

detail.title: Sensitization, delay discounting, and BMI percentile change over 24 months in adolescents from lower-income households
detail.abstract: Previous studies have shown that an increase in motivation for food (RVFOOD ) after repeated exposure, or sensitization, is associated with BMI percentile and BMI percentile change over time. The purpose of this study was to investigate the impact of food insecurity and delay discounting (DD) on this relationship. We recruited 118 adolescents aged 11 – 14 from moderate to lower income households, balanced for sex and household food insecurity status, 87 of whom completed 24 month follow-up. Height, weight, eating behavior, and DD were assessed at baseline and again after 6, 15, and 24 months. RVFOOD was measured before and after two weeks of daily consumption to assess sensitization. We assessed relationships among time, sensitization, food insecurity, DD and BMI percentile, controlling for child age and sex. We found that sensitization was associated with BMI percentile cross-sectionally, but was not associated with BMI percentile change over time. Food insecurity was not associated with BMI percentile change over time nor did it moderate the relationship between sensitization and BMI percentile. There was an association between DD and time on BMI percentile, but DD did not moderate the relationship between sensitization and BMI percentile. When taken together, sensitization is associated with BMI percentile in adolescents, but not changes in BMI percentile over time. The association between DD and BMI percentile varied over time, but was not consistent in strength or direction. These findings suggest that sensitization and DD may represent promising behavioral targets for future obesity-prevention interventions in at-risk adolescents.

title: LUSIM: An LLM-Driven Spatial-Equilibrium Simulator for Urban Planning

detail.title: LUSIM: An LLM-Driven Spatial-Equilibrium Simulator for Urban Planning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nan

detail.abstract: Quantitative ex-ante urban-policy evaluation has historically relied on closedform spatial-equilibrium and low-dimensional discrete-choice models that constrain analysis to homogeneous agents and fixed-form parametric utilities, and thereby to smooth proportional responses around the calibrated baseline. Integrating large language models into multi-agent simulation alleviates these constraints, but existing LLM-driven platforms lack the market-clearing mechanism and externally calibrated parameters that quantitative policy evaluation requires. We present LUSim (LLM-driven Urban Simulator), a multi-agent simulator in which heterogeneous households choose residence and workplace through a large language model and clear housing and labour markets inside an externally calibrated general-equilibrium city, with structural decision rules as baselines under identical conditions. We simulate a new rapid-transit line on a 96-zone Berlin instance calibrated from Ahlfeldt et al. (2015). The structural engines, which can only reweight the calibrated city in proportion, concentrate their response at the new stations, whereas with LLM-driven households approximately eight times as many relocate and the gains shift to peripheral districts. To test which engine predicts real urban change, we initialise every engine on the divided Berlin of 1986, let it predict the reunified city, and score, by criteria fixed in advance, its prediction of which districts gain or lose residents, jobs, prices, and wages against the changes observed by 2006. The simulation with LLM-driven households predicts these changes better than every structural baseline, also with district names withheld so that it cannot rely on memorised history, and the contrast persists across a second rail corridor, a zoning policy that expands floor space, and a second model family. We interpret these results as evidence that LLM-driven decision rules, disciplined by market clearing in a calibrated environment, predict urban change beyond the reach of structural models.

detail.abstract: Written communication promotes understanding, conveys authority, and inspires action. In organizations, emails often serve as a proxy for leadership presence by setting a tone, articulating expectations, and reinforcing organizational culture. Increasingly, however, this communication is no longer written solely by the sender. With a simple prompt, generative AI can instantly produce a confident response before we even have time to think or take a breath. detail.abstract: This monograph develops a biblical theology of discovery: the claim that human beings are called not only to inhabit and cultivate creation but also to attend to it, name it, learn its patterns, discern its possibilities, and use truthful knowledge in service of life, wisdom, justice, beauty, and worship. The argument begins with the distinction between creation and discovery. Human beings do not bring the fundamental realities of creation into existence; they encounter realities already given by God. Discovery therefore has a receptive character before it has an inventive one. Genesis presents human vocation as embodied, cognitive, linguistic, agricultural, relational, and cultural. Adam's naming of animals, the cultivation mandate, and the image-of-God commission establish a pattern in which human beings responsibly interpret and develop a world that is meaningful before they arrive. The wider canon deepens this pattern through wisdom's observation of creatures and consequences, Israel's calendars and attention to seasons, Solomon's study of plants and animals, Job's summons to learn from the nonhuman world, the technical artistry of Bezalel and Oholiab, medical and practical knowledge, navigation and astronomy, and the New Testament's affirmation that created realities can be known and received without being salvific in themselves. The monograph argues that astronomy, medicine, mathematics, craftsmanship, natural history, engineering, and related forms of inquiry can be understood as culturally elaborated expressions of the human vocation to know and steward creation, provided that discovery remains accountable to truth, creaturely limits, neighbor-love, justice, and worship. It also distinguishes general revelation from special revelation, discovery from redemption, knowledge from wisdom, and technological capacity from moral permission. A biblical theology of discovery thus neither divinizes science nor fears truthful inquiry. It treats disciplined discovery as a form of creaturely participation in a creation whose order, intelligibility, and fruitfulness originate in God.

detail.abstract: Short dramas attract large audiences, yet producers spend heavily on social media influencers to promote them. Research has examined influencer selection and effectiveness, but the allocation of short-drama promotion across influencers shared by competing producers over time remains underexplored. We develop a two-period game to guide these allocation decisions and derive a platform policy of charges and subsidies. We find that a drama can generate strong engagement yet receive too much promotion when it displaces content that better sustains future audience exposure. The policy restrains promotion that imposes net losses on competitors and supports promotion whose future benefits to them exceed their competitive losses. We apply the model to 123,362 promotions of 15,896 dramas on Douyin and Kuaishou. Reallocating existing promotion toward better-matched influencers and dramas with stronger predicted engagement raises the predicted current engagement index by 37.8%. A policy of limited charges and subsidies for future audience exposure yields nearly the same predicted performance as the optimized allocation, with only 7.0% of promotions requiring reassignment to reach that benchmark. These findings show how better allocation can improve the return from existing promotion and how platform pricing can support those improvements.

title: The End of Oil
affiliations: University of Chicago

detail.title: The End of Oil
detail.abstract:
It is now plausible to envision scenarios in which global demand for crude oil falls to essentially zero by the end of this century, driven by improvements in clean energy technologies, adoption of stringent climate policies, or both. This paper asks what such a demand decline, when anticipated, might mean for global oil supply. One possibility is the well-known “green paradox”: because oil is an exhaustible resource, producers may accelerate near-term extraction in order to beat the demand decline. This reaction would increase near-term CO2 emissions and could possibly even lead the total present value of climate damages to be greater than if demand had not declined at all. However, because oil extraction requires potentially long-lived investments in wells and other infrastructure, the opposite may occur: an anticipated demand decline reduces producers' investment rates, decreasing near-term oil production and CO2 emissions. To evaluate whether this disinvestment effect outweighs the green paradox, or vice-versa, I develop a tractable model of global oil supply that incorporates both effects, while also capturing industry features such as heterogeneous producers, exercise of market power by low-cost OPEC producers, and marginal drilling costs that increase with the rate of drilling. I find that for model inputs with the strongest empirical support, the disinvestment effect outweighs the traditional green paradox. In order for anticipation effects on net to substantially increase cumulative global oil extraction, I find that industry investments must have short time horizons, and that producers must have discount rates that are comparable to U.S. treasury bill rates.

detail.abstract: The commercialisation of Earth observation is transforming the regulatory subject of space law. Satellite-data markets now extend beyond ownership and operation of satellites to data reception, cloud access, distribution, resale, processing, analytics and satellite-derived information services. Nigeria illustrates the resulting regulatory challenge. The National Space Research and Development Agency Act 2010 gives the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) functions concerning satellite data and creates licensing and regulation-making powers capable of supporting aspects of satellite-data governance, while the Regulations on Licensing and Supervision of Space Activities 2015 remain predominantly organised around space objects and their operators. This article argues for a transition from asset-based space regulation to activity-based satellite-data regulation. It examines sections 6(k), 9 and 35 of the NASRDA Act, identifies gaps across the commercial satellite-data value chain, and draws comparative lessons from the United States, France and India. It proposes a technology-neutral and risk-differentiated framework governing acquisition, reception, commercial dissemination and security-sensitive processing according to activity, jurisdictional nexus and risk. It further argues that Nigeria should use existing statutory powers for immediately defensible downstream regulation while pursuing targeted legislative amendment for broader foreign-provider jurisdiction, investigative powers, substantial penalties and clearly defined offences. The proposed model seeks to strengthen regulatory certainty, national security and commercial development without creating a state monopoly over satellite information or unnecessarily restricting open Earth-observation data.

detail.abstract:
We present a system-neutral architecture for coupling smart-contract bonds to external payment or settlement systems. Participant-operated connectors link authenticated external-system access to participant-controlled on-chain oracle proxies, while an asset-agnostic settlement contract maintains the immutable transfer context. Building on ERC-7573, the design covers issuance, redemption, and coupon payment.

Coupons are modelled as payment-versus-discharge: the bond reserves the holder’s claim, freezes authentic receiver-domain outcome commitments, and records the claim as paid only after independently accepting the corresponding success preimage. Acceptance of the failure preimage closes the settlement attempt without discharging the claim. Under the stated initialisation, key-protection, outcome-release, and finality assumptions, settlement status alone cannot discharge a coupon.

We compare asset-side and cash-side locking and distinguish uncertain external-operation recovery from repeatable key relay. External success does not ensure completion on its own; completion additionally requires eventual key publication, relay, and successful acceptance by the bond.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural inadequacy of existing transnational criminal-law and financial-intelligence frameworks when confronted with autonomous, self-executing computational systems that launder illicit proceeds without a continuously identifiable human principal. It develops the concept of the personhood vacuum — the doctrinal gap opened when non-custodial DeFi mixers, autonomous cross-chain bridges, and weaponized generative-AI systems operate independently of their original developers — and traces its consequences across three domains: algorithmic money laundering under the FATF Travel Rule and the EU's MiCA Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114); the corruption of KYC identity verification through adversarial biometric deepfakes and the resulting Article 8 ECHR tensions raised by hybrid AI network countermeasures (Klass v. Germany; Big Brother Watch v. the United Kingdom; Van Buren v. United States); and the capacity of INTERPOL's constitutional mandate (Articles 2 and 3 of the INTERPOL Constitution) to accommodate state-sponsored algorithmic criminality such as Lazarus Group's exploitation of Tornado Cash, at issue in United States v. Roman Storm. Drawing on the English Commercial Court's proprietary injunction jurisprudence (AA v Persons Unknown; Fetch.ai v Persons Unknown) and the Bitfinex-hack recovery in United States v. Lichtenstein and Morgan, the paper argues for a doctrinal shift from prosecution oriented to forfeiture-oriented enforcement — in rem forfeiture against code — and proposes a concrete instrument, the INTERPOL International Protocol on Algorithmic Asset Forfeiture and Synthetic Evidence Verification, to operationalise this shift across member states.

detail.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled GIS agents to perform complex geospatial tasks, but autonomous operation remains constrained by data access. Existing approaches rely on source-specific curated resources that require manual authoring and validation, limiting scalability across heterogeneous data infrastructures. This study proposes an LLM-based framework for geospatial data source onboarding that enables agents to acquire, verify, and retain the operational knowledge needed to retrieve data from previously unintegrated sources and reuse that knowledge across tasks. We evaluated the framework through three experiments: 45 retrieval tasks across five access mechanisms with and without automatically generated handbooks, 15 tasks from the LLM-Find benchmark, and five autonomous end-to-end spatial analysis tasks. Results show that autonomously generated handbook guidance increased verified completion across the 45 retrieval tasks from 13 (28.9%) to 35 (77.8%), improving performance across all five access mechanisms. Handbooks also supported successful retrieval in 13 of 15 LLM-Find benchmark tasks. Required data were successfully retrieved for all five spatial analyses, although one case required intervention. By enabling GIS agents to automatically acquire source-specific knowledge, retain it for reuse, and integrate it into GIS workflows, the framework provides a concrete pathway toward self-growing data retrieval capabilities in Autonomous GIS.

detail.abstract: The regulation of non-consensual intimate deepfakes reveals a transatlantic schism between protecting the dignity of the person depicted and protecting the liberty of the speaker. While the US Take It Down Act remains tethered to analogue-era concepts of specific intent and visual deception, the United Kingdom, through the Online Safety Act 2023 and section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, has pivoted towards a rights-based conception of sexual autonomy. The paper compares the two frameworks along three axes. It begins with mens rea, contrasting the United Kingdom's consent-based offence, under which the non-consensual sharing itself grounds liability, with the American requirement of an intent to cause harm, which opens a 'satire loophole'. It then examines the actus reus, arguing that the US insistence that a forgery be 'indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction' treats the wrong as a deception of the viewer rather than a violation of the victim and leaves 'cheapfake' victims unprotected, before contrasting the Take It Down Act's forty-eight-hour removal mandate with the Online Safety Act's ex ante safety duties. A blind spot common to both jurisdictions is then identified: the 'tool gap', whereby liability attaches to the user who publishes while the developers of abuse-generating tools remain largely unregulated. Effective protection requires a hybrid model that joins British substantive definitions to American procedural speed, reinforced by cryptographic provenance standards and by liability extending upstream to the developers of these tools.

detail.title: How Does Government Borrowing Affect Corporate Financing and Investment?
detail.abstract: Using a novel dataset of accounting and market information that spans most publicly traded nonfinancial firms over the last century, we show that U.S. federal government debt issuance significantly affects corporate financial policies and balance sheets through its impact on investors' portfolio allocations and the relative pricing of different assets. Government debt is strongly negatively correlated with corporate debt and investment, but strongly positively correlated with corporate liquidity. These relations are more pronounced in larger, less risky firms whose debt is a closer substitute for Treasuries. Indeed, we find a strong negative relation between the BAA-AAA yield spread and government debt, highlighting the greater sensitivity of more highly rated credit to variation in the supply of Treasuries. The channel through which this effect operates is investors' portfolio decisions: domestic intermediaries actively substitute between lending to the federal government and the nonfinancial corporate sector. The relations between government debt and corporate policies, as well as the substitution between government and corporate debt by intermediaries, are stronger after 1970 when foreign demand increased competition for Treasury securities. In concert, our results suggest that large, financially healthy corporations act as liquidity providers by supplying relatively safe securities to investors when alternatives are in short supply, and that this financial strategy influences firms' capital structures and investment policies.

detail.abstract:
This monograph develops a doctrinal and methodological framework for regulating automated decision-making where algorithmic outputs produce legally binding or otherwise legally consequential effects.

The study proceeds from the premise that automation does not remove the legal requirements applicable to public decision-making. Where computational systems perform functions previously exercised by human officials, requirements concerning accuracy, auditability, explainability, evidentiary reliability, and meaningful human control must remain capable of legal verification. To address the resulting gap between legal requirements and technical implementation, the monograph develops a two-plane method connecting the normative and technical dimensions of algorithmic decision-making. Legal requirements are translated into engineering specifications and subsequently assessed through measurable coefficients.

The proposed framework introduces four principal coefficients—accuracy, auditability, explainability, and human override—and combines them into the Algorithmic Legitimacy and Measurability coefficient (KAEMK_{AEM}). A threshold of 0.30 is proposed as a calibrated operational boundary for retrospective analysis and as a possible de lege ferenda mechanism for determining whether an automated system should be permitted to produce legally consequential outputs. The monograph expressly distinguishes this proposed threshold from existing positive law and treats it as a methodological construct requiring further empirical and doctrinal validation.

The study further develops the doctrines of algorithmic legal fact, phantom fact, evidentiary integrity, algorithmic opportunism, temporal continuity of legitimacy, the infrastructure anchor, the Hardware Circuit Breaker, and the Sovereign Gateway. Four documented cases—COMPAS, SyRI, the Post Office Horizon litigation, and Robodebt—are examined retrospectively as stress tests of the proposed methodology. Their function is not to establish a universally valid legal constant, but to examine whether the proposed framework produces coherent classifications across materially different forms of automated decision-making failure.

The monograph also reconstructs a broader genealogy of the problem, connecting contemporary debates on automated decision-making and technological due process with earlier discussions of cybernetics, material truth, human responsibility, and the limits of transferring legally significant judgment to computational systems.

The principal contribution of the study is the integration of legal doctrine and technical measurement into a common analytical protocol: a legal requirement is translated into a technical criterion, measured through defined parameters, aggregated into a legitimacy coefficient, and connected to a proposed legal consequence. The framework thereby seeks to make the legitimacy of automated public decision-making not merely a matter of procedural assertion, but an object capable of doctrinal specification, technical verification, and measurable calibration.

detail.abstract: Menstrual stigma is pervasive in low-and middle-income countries, yet we know little about its consequences for girls' human capital. In a field experiment in 140 schools in Madagascar (N =2,256), we evaluate a school hygiene program focused on reducing menstrual stigma through sanitation infrastructure, menstrual products, and teacher-and peer-led sensitization. The program generates substantial learning gains (0.15 SD) without improving attendance or health. The learning gains are instead explained by psychosocial mechanisms: reduced stigma, lower stress measured by heart rate, and a better school social climate. Our results suggest that menstruation can be a meaningful barrier to girls' learning.

detail.abstract: Irregular migration to Europe by sea, though risky, remains one of the most popular migration options for many Sub-Saharan Africans. This study examines the drivers of irregular migration decisions using an incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment in rural Gambia, the African country with the highest per-capita rate of irregular migration to Europe. Potential migrants substantially overestimate the probability of dying en route, reporting an average belief of 51 percent compared with a best available estimate of about 20 percent. In the experiment, reducing the probability of dying en route from 50 to 20 percent raises willingness to migrate irregularly by 3.0 percentage points, while reducing the probability of obtaining legal residence from 50 to 30 percent lowers it by 2.1 points. Our results highlight the importance of potential migrants' prior beliefs in shaping responses to information and suggest that information policies that fail to account for these beliefs may backfire.

title: From External Inputs to Domestic Capability: Systemic Absorption in Late Industrialization
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: From External Inputs to Domestic Capability: Systemic Absorption in Late Industrialization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Late industrialization often begins by importing what the domestic economy does not yet possess: capital, machinery, technical knowledge, management, standards, foreign investment, and access to global markets. The developmental question is not whether these inputs arrive, but whether repeated use changes the receiving production system.

This paper distinguishes input absorption from systemic absorption. Input absorption occurs when an imported resource can be used. Systemic absorption occurs when repeated use leaves behind reproducible domestic capabilities: maintenance, supplier formation, worker and engineer circulation, local technical services, financing competence, and the ability to replicate or adapt production without reconstructing the original external package. 

The paper identifies four conversion mechanisms-learning through repeated operation, supplier formation, labor circulation, and institutional adaptation-and proposes four tests of absorption: operation, maintenance, replication, and adaptation. The distinction is not between dependence and self-sufficiency. A deeply capable economy may remain highly dependent on imported inputs by choice. The relevant criterion is optionality: whether external specialization rests on internal competence or substitutes for it.

The framework yields a prospective research design. Early indicators of maintenance localization, supplier entry, technical labor mobility, and institutional adaptation should predict later replication and adaptation after foreign partners withdraw, change terms, or cease to provide critical functions. Systemic absorption is therefore treated as a conversion process rather than a territorial presence effect.

title: Learning from Coworkers: Peer Effects on Individual Investment Decisions
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Finance Area

detail.title: Learning from Coworkers: Peer Effects on Individual Investment Decisions
detail.abstract: We use unique data on employee decisions in the employee stock purchase plans (ESPPs) of U.S. public firms to measure the influence of networks on investment decisions. Comparing only employees within a firm during the same election window and controlling for a metro area fixed effect, we find that the local choices of coworkers to participate in the firm’s ESPP exert a significant influence on employees’ own decisions to participate. Local coworkers’ trading patterns also disseminate to colleagues through the network. In the cross-section, we find that some employees (men, younger workers) are particularly susceptible to peer influence. Generally, we find that more similar employees exert greater influence on each other’s decisions and, particularly, that high (low) information employees are most affected by other high (low) information employees. However, we also find that the presence of high information employees magnifies the effects of peer networks. We trace a value-increasing investment choice through employee networks. Thus, our analysis suggests the potential of networks and targeted investor education to improve financial decision-making.

detail.abstract: This paper examines variation in gender gaps in mathematics across economies, with a particular focus on high-achieving students who are more likely to become future innovators in STEM fields. Using pooled microdata from the 2012, 2015, 2018 and 2022 waves of the OECD Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), covering more than two million students across advanced economies and emerging markets, the documents in a number of stylized facts. Female students tend to underperform male students in mathematics on average and outperform in reading. The average gender gap in maths performance widens substantially towards the upper tail of the distribution of test scores. This widening of the gender gaps is significantly less pronounced in post-communist economies in Emerging Europe and Central Asia than in advanced economies and other emerging markets, resulting in a more balanced gender representation among the highest-achieving students. This lasting legacy of strong and relatively egalitarian maths tuition under central planning remains a potential source of competitive advantage for these economies.

title: Risk Aversion, Bluffing Strategy, and Financial Portfolio Choice: A Game-Theoretic and Behavioral Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not undergo formal institutional ethics review. The survey was anonymous and voluntary, collected no identifying information, involved only hypothetical payoffs with no real monetary stakes, and posed no foreseeable risk to participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the connection between risk aversion and strategic decision-making in poker, and argues that the same logic governing bluffing decisions also governs financial portfolio choice. Rather than assuming how an opponent responds to bets, we ground the response in a Bayesian Nash equilibrium: the opponent updates beliefs via Bayes's rule and acts according to a pot-odds indifference condition. Solving the model numerically across a range of risk-aversion levels reveals a clean result. The equilibrium mixing frequency contains no risk-aversion parameter, so risk aversion cannot operate through the rate at which weak hands are bluffed. It operates instead through two other channels: the size of the bet placed, and the binary question of whether to include bluffs in the betting range at all. That participation decision collapses sharply at a critical level of risk aversion rather than declining gradually, while bet size adjusts continuously on either side of the threshold. The abrupt exit is consistent with flight-to-safety dynamics in financial markets (Brunnermeier & Nagel, 2008). A behavioral survey of 55 participants, analysed at the level of the individual bluffing decision with scenario fixed effects, corroborates the theoretical predictions: a onepoint increase in self-reported risk tolerance raises the odds of bluffing by roughly 79 percent. Together, the formal model and survey evidence suggest that poker strategy and financial portfolio choice are two instances of the same underlying optimization problem.

detail.abstract: On-demand meal delivery platforms must jointly determine courier supply and bundle capacity, which sets the maximum number of active orders that a courier may carry. Increasing bundle capacity can improve courier productivity but may also lengthen the time from pickup to delivery. We develop a semi-Markov model that links kitchen-specific order destinations to the courier's active bundle and captures the sequence and timing of pickups and deliveries. The model is estimated and validated using Meituan data. With the baseline courier supply, increasing bundle capacity from one to four raises productivity from 2.98 to 3.96 orders per courier-hour, whereas further increases yield little additional gain. Higher bundle capacity nevertheless lengthens delivery time, revealing a tension between courier productivity and delivery performance. With more couriers available, a lower bundle capacity can meet the aggregate service capacity target relative to the incoming order rate. These findings show that bundle capacity and courier supply should be coordinated rather than determined separately. The model provides a unified framework for evaluating how these decisions jointly affect productivity, delivery performance, and system capacity.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the operational architecture and payment ecosystem dynamics of legacy retail ecosystems within emerging, rapidly formalizing economies. Focusing on the Chatuchak Market in Bangkok, Thailand, this forensic audit examines how informal and semi-formal vendors navigate formal digital banking infrastructure. Utilizing primary ethnographic fieldwork and transaction cost economics, the research isolates two primary mechanisms driving merchant resilience: the "Micro-Showroom" hybrid model-which leverages tourist foot traffic for unrecorded B2B manufacturing contracts-and aggressive transaction cost arbitrage. The study explores the microeconomic friction generated by international credit card networks versus the seamless adoption of the state-backed PromptPay system. The findings demonstrate that merchants within the audited wholesale-retail cluster consistently apply a 3% surcharge on credit card transactions to pass Merchant Discount Rates (MDR) to consumers, while accepting PromptPay as a zero-friction cash equivalent. Ultimately, this paper argues that Chatuchak is not a primitive tourist bazaar, but a hyper-rational, self-regulating wholesale portal that strategically absorbs formal payment channels only when financial intermediation costs approach zero.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is a corporate strategy used to align brand identity with changes in the business environment; however, changing a brand name can also create risks to brand equity and product competitiveness. This paper aims to analyze rebranding from the perspectives of marketing theory, regulatory pressures, legal aspects, and brand equity transfer. The discussion employs a multidimensional approach by examining Brand Equity, Brand Rebranding and Identity Matrix, International Marketing, and Brand Evolutionary Theory, and then relating these theories to several cases, including Mako/BreadTalk, AZKO/ACE Hardware, WWE/WWF, Geprek Bensu, Sony, Snickers, Bank Syariah Indonesia, and Hungry Jack's. The analysis shows that rebranding can enhance competitiveness through image renewal, market segmentation expansion, strategic efficiency, and opportunities for diversification. However, changes in identity also risk causing brand disconnection, consumer confusion, and increased communication costs. Therefore, successful rebranding depends on brand equity auditing, regulatory mapping, continuity of quality, retention of visual elements, precise communication, and financial readiness during the transition while remaining oriented toward consumer needs.

The author has no financial relationship with any company whose data are cited in this paper, including Semrush, Ahrefs, Profound, Similarweb, Peec AI, Evertune, Tinuiti, Conductor, Goodie AI, Yext, Muck Rack, BrightEdge, OtterlyAI, SparkToro or Gumshoe. detail.abstract: Published studies report sharply different answers about which websites generative AI search engines cite, often because they measure different denominators, selection stages and source universes. One widely shared figure places Reddit at about 40% of citations, another holds that the most-cited domain rarely exceeds 5%, and a third claims that YouTube has overtaken Reddit. This paper reports a structured secondary review of 30 evidence sources published between 2025 and September 2026, covering ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Claude. Each headline figure was traced to its original publisher and coded for metric definition, selection stage, engine, prompt universe, time window, collection method, counting unit and sponsor. Most of the disagreement comes from measurement choices. The same Profound dataset gives Wikipedia 7.8% of all ChatGPT citations but 47.9% of citations within ChatGPT's top-ten domain set. Semrush's widely quoted Reddit values sum to 208%, so they cannot be shares of all citations. YouTube's rise was measured within social citations, which formed only about 4% to 7% of all citations. After reconciliation, three broad findings are reasonably well supported. Engines differ in source mix, query type changes that mix, and citation shares move in steps after access and retrieval changes. Two conflicts remain unresolved. The paper offers a reconciliation checklist, a brand investment framework, six testable propositions and a design for a preregistered panel study.

detail.abstract: Occupational exposure indices measure what generative AI could do, not what it is used for. I build a behavioral measure of realized AI adoption from the Anthropic Economic Index and compare it with the standard exposure index across 47 occupational sectors. Adoption and exposure rank occupations alike but diverge in level, because adoption is far more concentrated. In weekly Indeed job postings after ChatGPT, labor demand tracks adoption rather than exposure: a one standard deviation increase in adoption predicts a decline of about 10 log points, while exposure adds nothing. Realized adoption captures AI's early labor market footprint.

title: The 2022–24 Yield Curve False Alarm and the Limits of Break Tests

detail.abstract: From November 2022 to November 2024, the 3-month Treasury bill yield was above the 10-year Treasury yield in every month, and a probit model of the spread, estimated each month on past data, put the probability of a recession 12 months ahead as high as 77 percent. No recession followed. Measured by average over-prediction over 36 months, this was the largest miss in the model's record since 1964, though only narrowly larger than its misses in its first years of forecasting. Sup-LR tests with simulated p-values detect no change in the coefficient on the spread, and they detect a lower intercept after 2008 only when unobserved recession risk is given the least persistence I consider. Power simulations show, however, that if recession risk is as persistent as the length of recessions suggests, the tests could not have detected a break of the size estimated after 2008. The evidence therefore cannot settle whether the relationship changed.

title: China’s Low-Altitude Economy: A Strategic Push and its Implications for Korea
affiliations: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade

detail.title: China’s Low-Altitude Economy: A Strategic Push and its Implications for Korea
detail.abstract:
China’s low-altitude economy is an emerging composite industry centered on the low-altitude flight of manned and unmanned aircraft, including drones (unmanned aerial vehicles, or UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and combined with applied services in logistics, tourism, and urban management.

Since its elevation to a national strategic industry in 2024, policy, markets, and technology have advanced together at an accelerating pace, and being written into the 15th Five-Year Plan as a strategic emerging industry in 2025 has established it as a medium- to long-term national strategy. The market is expanding quickly, from CNY 670 billion in 2024 to roughly CNY 1.5 trillion, or about KRW 280 trillion, in 2025, and routine operations are spreading through logistics, tourism, and urban management.

The industry’s development rests above all on a three-tier division of labor that binds three things into a single working structure: institutional and standards design by the central government, pilot zones operated by local governments, and technology and service delivery by private fi rms. Korea has strong technological capabilities in drones and urban air mobility (UAM), but gaps remain in institutions, infrastructure, and supply chains.

Drawing on China’s experience, Korea needs to consider, step by step, building institutional foundations ahead of deployment, establishing city-scale demonstration systems, and pursuing cooperation on international certification.

title: Energy Security Risk and a Green Transition Strategy for Korean Industry
affiliations: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade

detail.title: Energy Security Risk and a Green Transition Strategy for Korean Industry
detail.abstract:
The continuing military confrontation between the US and Iran has produced an energy shock much like the one of 2022. That shock exposes a structural vulnerability rooted in the gap between the pace at which fossil fuel systems are being wound down and the pace at which renewable systems are being built, and it makes the case for re-examining the green transition as a question of resilience under external shock rather than one of speed.

Korea carries what this study calls a triple exposure structure: high energy import dependence, a large manufacturing share, and a high share of energy consumed by industry. That combination leaves the country especially vulnerable to a vicious circle in which energy price shocks erode corporate profitability and then depress investment. Operating margins at energy-intensive fi rms did in fact fall during the 2022 crisis.

Major economies have each mobilized fiscal and financial instruments against transition risk in their own way, but Korea’s fiscal capacity and manufacturing-centered industrial structure limit how far those approaches can simply be transplanted. This study therefore proposes a risk-responsive transition strategy built on three axes: stabilizing costs in the short term by improving how industrial electricity tariff s are operated; securing investment capacity in the medium term by making transition fi nance effective and introducing carbon contracts for difference; and upgrading the industrial structure over the long term by accelerating the shift toward high-value-added industries.

title: Regret Equals Covariance: A Characterization for Stochastic Optimization
affiliations: Risk AI Center (RiskAICenter.com) -- Advancing the science of AI in finance: Independent research center and executive education institute.

detail.title: Regret Equals Covariance: A Characterization for Stochastic Optimization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A

detail.abstract: Quantifying regret typically involves repeatedly resolving a stochastic optimization problem across simulated scenarios. Such an approach is costly: the cost scales with the number of scenarios and the cost of each solve. We propose that regret can instead be measured using the joint moments of the cost vector c and the optimal decision π * (c). Working with the optimal concave and Lipschitz under only a feasible region value function v(c) = min z∈Z c ⊤ z, we show that regret always decomposes as Regret =-Cov(c, π * (c))-R(c) for a residual R(c). We further show that R(c) = 0 when π * is affine in c, which holds for unconstrained and equality-constrained (e.g., budget-constrained Markowitz) quadratic programs and many, but not all, linear programs. For all cases, we give a distribution-free bound Regret ≤ D √︁ tr(Σ c) that depends only on the radius of the feasible region and the cost covariance. We also derive concentration and asymptotic-normality results for the empirical regret, the latter under an explicit and checkable non-degeneracy condition.

title: Korea-India Industrial Collaboration: Driving Shared Growth and Future Prosperity
affiliations: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade and Institute for Studies in Industrial Development

detail.title: Korea-India Industrial Collaboration: Driving Shared Growth and Future Prosperity
detail.abstract:
This volume represents the second collaborative publication produced under the KIET–ISID partnership, which seeks to promote policy dialogue and strengthen economic and industrial cooperation between Korea and India. 

The first part of the volume explores the evolving Korea–India economic partnership in the context of changing global economic conditions. The chapters examine foreign direct investment trends, emerging geopolitical challenges, and the implications of recent changes in the international economic order for bilateral cooperation.

The second part focuses on labor-intensive industries and digital transformation. These chapters discuss opportunities for cooperation in employment-intensive manufacturing sectors, SME development, and emerging digital technologies that can contribute to inclusive growth and industrial upgrading. 

The third part examines strategic industries that are expected to play an increasingly important role in the future of Korea–India cooperation. Particular attention is given to sectors such as shipbuilding and steel, where complementarities between the two economies create opportunities for long-term industrial collaboration.

The volume concludes with “The Way Forward,” which synthesizes the key findings and policy recommendations presented throughout the volume and proposes a framework for advancing Korea–India industrial cooperation in the years ahead.

We hope that this volume will contribute to a deeper understanding of the opportunities and challenges facing Korea–India relations and serve as a useful reference for policymakers, researchers, industry stakeholders, and all those interested in advancing a stronger and more resilient Korea–India partnership.

title: Crisis or Turning Point? Energy Storage and the Next Growth Engine for Korea’s Battery Industry
affiliations: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade

detail.title: Crisis or Turning Point? Energy Storage and the Next Growth Engine for Korea’s Battery Industry
detail.abstract:
Talk of a crisis in Korea’s battery industry has not subsided. Slowing demand for electric vehicles, China’s expanding market share, and mounting policy uncertainty in major economies have arrived together, and the earnings of Korean firms have suffered as a result. What deserves attention, however, is that this recent weakness does not stem from any stagnation in the global battery industry. World battery demand continues to rise in existing markets, on the intensive margin, and demand in new applications, on the extensive margin, has lately been expanding quickly.

This paper shows that the root cause of the crisis in Korea’s battery industry lies not in the electric vehicle chasm itself but in an erosion of competitiveness in the country’s core market and core product. It further argues that the industry’s center of growth is shifting structurally from electric vehicles to energy storage systems (ESS), and it focuses on the US ESS market, which is growing on the strength of expanding renewable generation and the spread of AI data centers. The United States is combining tariff policy with the supply chain restrictions attached to the advanced manufacturing production credit (AMPC) to reduce its reliance on Chinese ESS and build a supply chain centered on itself. These policy changes are expected to open new growth opportunities for Korean battery firms that have established production bases on US soil.

ESS is critical infrastructure underpinning the global energy transition and the spread of the AI industry. Building ESS into a new engine of growth for Korea’s battery industry will require using US supply chain policy strategically, and it will also require expanded policy support to strengthen the domestic battery materials industry, to upgrade the systems through which Korea responds to industrial and trade policy in major economies, and to build capability in next-generation ESS technology and system integration (SI).

title: Stock Price Informativeness, Managerial Horizon, and Dynamic Incentive Provision
affiliations: University of Oregon, Lundquist School of Business

detail.title: Stock Price Informativeness, Managerial Horizon, and Dynamic Incentive Provision
detail.abstract: This paper examines how stock-price informativeness shapes the effectiveness of price-based managerial compensation. As rational forecasts of value formed through trading, stock prices move one-for-one with publicly observed macroeconomic shocks but reflect managerial actions only partially, making the price a natural benchmark for ongoing performance yet a limited measure of past effort. Because sequentially optimal contracts overexploit the price as a forward-looking benchmark, greater informativeness can discourage long-tenured managers from creating long-term value. The mix of macroeconomic and firm-specific risk governs this trade-off: it determines whether managerial incentives strengthen or weaken with firm-specific risk, and whether firm value is maximized at an intermediate level of informativeness or at an extreme. Informativeness also plays a distributive role, transferring wealth from liquidity traders to informed speculators. Because that transfer is largest at intermediate informativeness, the socially optimal degree of informativeness can depart from the level that maximizes firm value.

title: Unexpected work capacity reductions and analyst research productivity
affiliations: Bayes Business School, City University London, Washington University in St. Louis, Lancaster University - Lancaster University Management School and Lancaster University - Lancaster University Management School

detail.title: Unexpected work capacity reductions and analyst research productivity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: We examine how sell-side analysts reallocate research capacity during unexpected, temporary capacity shocks, proxied by weekly influenza intensity in the state where analysts work. Rather than cutting output uniformly, analysts pause forecast updates for small, less widely followed stocks while maintaining forecast volume for larger stocks that are more widely followed, even as forecast quality falls. For the stocks they continue to cover, analysts substitute long-term for short-term  forecasts, reducing the short-term share of their forecasts by four percentage points and shifting research output toward horizons where inaccuracy is less salient to investors. The substitution effect is stronger when blockholder ownership is higher and weaker when analysts have more resources, face more competition, are newly hired, or can rely on management guidance. Forecast output begins to recover within two weeks, and the horizon shift is no longer statistically detectable by the third week. Among analysts who change brokerage houses, those who maintain a short-term-heavy mix during high-flu weeks are more likely to move to a smaller brokerage house. When the analysts covering a firm face higher flu intensity, trading volume falls, bid-ask spreads widen, and transient institutional ownership declines. Our results suggest that when analysts face temporary capacity constraints, they manage their output to minimize reputational damage, with real consequences for the information environment of the firms they cover.

title: Selective Learning from Extreme Observations in Dynamic Model Averaging

detail.abstract: Adaptive forecasting is most difficult when an exceptional observation is informative but its persistence is unknown. I develop bounded-influence dynamic model averaging (BI-DMA), which applies no bounded-influence weight to model-probability or observation-variance learning and bounds only the leverage of extreme innovations on persistent coefficient-state updates. Across 201 U.S. quarterly macroeconomic and financial targets and horizons from one to eight quarters, standard DMA often improves typical forecast accuracy yet remains exposed to rare, exceptionally large squared errors. A learning-channel decomposition locates this fragility in unrestricted coefficient-state adaptation rather than model-probability learning. BI-DMA alters only about 1.1-1.3% of coefficient-state updates and substantially reduces forecast-tail exposure. Simulations show that this protection need not impede adaptation to persistent coefficient breaks or changing predictor relevance. The results support selective, rather than symmetric, adaptation under instability.

detail.abstract: The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism entered its definitive phase in January 2026, and free allowances for covered sectors are withdrawn in full by 2034. Existing assessments rely on computable general equilibrium models calibrated at sector or macro level under fixed price assumptions. We provide the first installation-level microsimulation of the phaseout, projecting compliance costs for each of the roughly 9,800 active EU ETS stationary installations over 2025-2034. Each installation enters with its observed expanded dynamic allowance balance, constructed in a companion paper, rather than with a modelled emission intensity. Emission paths are projected plant by plant under three scenarios, and the allowance price follows a mean-reverting jump-diffusion calibrated to 2013-2025 EUA dynamics and simulated 100,000 times for each of four long-run targets between e60 and e150; costs are therefore distributions rather than point forecasts. Against a counterfactual of unchanged free allocation, the CBAM-attributable increment is concentrated in a few sectors and its timing is governed not by the common withdrawal schedule but by the year each sector's inherited bank runs out. The compliance-only balance used in the existing literature understates that increment and mis-times the exhaustion by up to three and a half years.

detail.abstract: High-mix manufacturers need production plans that remain executable when machine compatibility, mold changes, delivery windows, and accessory synchronization are made explicit. This paper studies the problem as production-envelope refinement. A planning layer constructs machine-day commitments for production, fulfillment, inventory, outsourcing, unmet demand, and mold states. A stable constructive scheduler then refines those commitments into order-level machine-day allocations under a one-mold-per-machine-per-day rule. The scheduler maintains residual invariants over fulfillment, production, and capacity; when all fulfillment residuals are discharged, the returned allocation is executable with respect to the stated production envelope. The method is evaluated on a factory-provided anonymized smartphone-case manufacturing scenario with 37 product types, 150 orders, and more than 8.3 million requested units. Under the scenario semantics used to construct the envelopeincluding the declared initial-inventory and external-accessory-supply interpretation, effective machine capacities, due windows, divisible order quantities, and planned mold-state sequence-Scheme C reports 100% on-time delivery, zero modeled shell outsourcing, and 1.9-4.6% changeover-driven capacity loss. These are scenario-calibrated results, not an independent plant-performance audit; a separate strict zero-inventory audit of the same workbook yields an accessory load ratio of 8.08 and cannot establish full internal completion under that narrower feasible set. The unstable machine-level ablation leaves 40 orders not internally completed within the due window and requires outsourced production. A separate 4-profile, 3-size, 30-seed, 3-budget synthetic matrix compares the method with EDD, ATCS, RH-EDD, and RH-CP-SAT under shared capacity, compatibility, and completion definitions. The proposed refinement is competitive in 30-order instances, reaching 99.5% mean completion at 30-60 s with fewer changeovers in the evaluated cases, whereas due-date dispatching achieves higher completion in 150-order stress cases. These results support a bounded contribution: production-envelope refinement gives a verifiable planning-to-execution interface, preserves planned mold-state stability, and reports residual bottlenecks, while completion depends on load and compatibility regimes.
